# Sanctum Runtime
# https://www.sanctumruntime.com/llms.txt

> Sanctum Runtime is the runtime trust boundary for autonomous systems.
> It sits between AI reasoning and real-world execution — approve, pause,
> or block actions before side effects happen.

## What it is

Open-source (MIT) middleware that gates any action — tool calls, robot commands,
API writes, file operations, smart home devices, industrial controls — with a
policy engine, optional human approval, signed action tokens, and an audit trail.

Not a chat guardrail. Not an LLM wrapper. The boundary at execution time.

## Full documentation (LLM-optimized, ~30 sections)

https://www.sanctumruntime.com/llms-full.txt

## Quick start

  npm install @sanctum-runtime/sdk @sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime

  import { SanctumRuntime } from '@sanctum-runtime/sdk'
  import { protectAgent } from '@sanctum-runtime/adapter-agent-runtime'

  const sanctum = new SanctumRuntime({ baseUrl: process.env.SANCTUM_API_URL! })

  await protectAgent(sanctum, {
    actor: 'my-agent',
    action: 'send_email',
    context: { to: 'user@example.com' },
    execute: async () => sendEmail(),
  })

## Core API

  POST /v1/actions/verify   — gate an action → APPROVED | REQUIRE_VERIFICATION | BLOCKED
  GET  /v1/audit            — audit log
  POST /v1/policies         — create/update policy
  GET  /v1/evidence/summary — SOC2 / NIST AI RMF control evidence

## Connect Agent (zero-install proxy)

Route external AI agents (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Doubao, Gemini)
through Sanctum by changing base_url — no SDK installation required:

  base_url: https://api.sanctumruntime.com/v1/proxy/openai
  header:   X-Sanctum-Agent-Token: sk_agent_...
